## Solution

The statement is **true**.

### Proof

Let $\mathbb{R}^I$ be endowed with the product topology. We establish the result by proving the contrapositive:

> If $P_J(x) \in P_J(\Omega)$ for **every** finite $J \subset I$, then $x \in \Omega$.

**Step 1: Characterizing closure via finite projections.**

A basic open neighborhood of $x$ in the product topology has the form
$$P_J^{-1}(V) = \prod_{i\in I} U_i, \qquad U_i = \mathbb{R} \text{ for } i\notin J,$$
where $J\subset I$ is finite and $V\subset \mathbb{R}^J$ is an open neighborhood of $P_J(x)$. Therefore
$$x\in \overline{\Omega} \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \bigl[\forall\text{ finite }J,\;\forall\text{ open }V\ni P_J(x)\text{ in }\mathbb{R}^J:\; P_J^{-1}(V)\cap\Omega\neq\emptyset\bigr].$$
The condition on the right is equivalent to: for every finite $J$, every open neighborhood of $P_J(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^J$ meets $P_J(\Omega)$, i.e.
$$x\in\overline{\Omega} \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \forall\text{ finite }J\subset I:\; P_J(x)\in\overline{P_J(\Omega)}. \tag{$\ast$}$$

**Step 2: $\Omega$ is closed.**

$\mathbb{R}^I$ with the product topology is Hausdorff (a product of Hausdorff spaces is Hausdorff). A compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed, so $\Omega$ is closed, i.e. $\overline{\Omega}=\Omega$.

**Step 3: Each $P_J(\Omega)$ is closed.**

The projection $P_J:\mathbb{R}^I\to\mathbb{R}^J$ is continuous (projections are continuous in the product topology). The continuous image of a compact set is compact, so $P_J(\Omega)$ is compact in $\mathbb{R}^J$. Since $\mathbb{R}^J$ is Hausdorff, $P_J(\Omega)$ is closed, i.e. $\overline{P_J(\Omega)}=P_J(\Omega)$.

**Step 4: Conclusion.**

Combining Steps 2 and 3 with $(\ast)$:
$$x\in\Omega \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \forall\text{ finite }J\subset I:\; P_J(x)\in P_J(\Omega).$$

Taking the contrapositive:
$$x\notin\Omega \;\Longrightarrow\; \exists\text{ finite }J\subset I:\; P_J(x)\notin P_J(\Omega).$$

This is precisely the statement to be proved. $\blacksquare$
